papers.title: An Essential Role of the AMPK-Related Kinase Snrk in Regulating Drosophila Sleep.
papers.summary: The paper reports that knockout of the AMPK-related kinase Snrk in Drosophila causes a profound loss of night-time sleep, much stronger than sik3 mutants, and that Snrk functions in cholinergic neurons to regulate sleep, with rescue by nicotinic acetylcholine receptor blockade.

papers.title: Novelty and anxiety differentially shape hippocampal assembly reactivation and sequence replay during REM sleep
papers.summary: This study combined calcium imaging and electrophysiology in mouse hippocampal CA1 neurons to detect reactivation during REM sleep. They found that structured waking activity is re-expressed during REM sleep, with novel experience enhancing sequential replay and anxiogenic experience increasing assembly reactivation frequency.

papers.title: Arrhythmic zone: When circadian clocks go quiet in the cold.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence for an 'arrhythmic zone' where circadian clocks fail at low temperatures across diverse organisms, discussing candidate mechanisms and adaptive significance. It highlights that circadian rhythms can weaken or disappear at temperatures within the organism's survival range.

papers.title: Nutritional Regulation of DN1a-Dh44 Signaling Modulates Sleep Across the Lifespan
papers.summary: This study shows that dietary sugar regulates sleep plasticity in Drosophila larvae and adults via CCHamide-1 signaling between DN1a and Dh44 neurons, independent of anatomical connectivity, with Dh44 neurons adjusting CCHa1-R mRNA levels in response to sugar.

papers.title: Orexin Signaling, Glymphatic Clearance, and Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease: A Scoping Review and Hypothesis-Generating Conceptual Framework.
papers.summary: This scoping review evaluates evidence linking orexin signaling, glymphatic clearance, and preclinical Alzheimer's disease. It found limited human evidence for disease-modifying effects of dual orexin receptor antagonists, with preclinical findings preliminary and lacking human validation.

papers.title: REV-Erbα as a Transcriptional Regulator Linking Circadian Rhythm, Metabolism, and Inflammation.
papers.journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets
papers.summary: This review focuses on the regulatory role of the nuclear receptor REV-ERBα in energy metabolism and inflammation, linking circadian rhythm disruption to chronic inflammatory conditions such as muscle wasting. It suggests REV-ERBα as a potential therapeutic target for metabolic and inflammatory diseases.

papers.title: Platinum-nanostructured silicon microneedles with scalable fabrication for EEG biosensing.
papers.summary: The paper describes a scalable fabrication method for platinum-nanostructured silicon microneedle electrode arrays that enhance EEG signal acquisition, increasing electroactive area ~15-fold and yielding higher signal-to-noise ratios than bare microneedles or gel-based electrodes, with improved user comfort.

papers.title: Evolving epileptic activity under focal rhythmic Delta activity: insights from simultaneous intracranial and scalp EEG.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of six patients with simultaneous scalp and intracranial EEG found that focal rhythmic delta activity (RDA) on scalp EEG reflects intracranial epileptic activity, including spikes and polyspikes, but not electrographic seizures or high-frequency oscillations, suggesting focal RDA as a potential target for antiseizure therapy.

papers.title: Normative Modeling of EEG Complexity Reveals Cortical Rigidity Associated with Pain Severity in Chronic Pain.
papers.summary: This study applied normative modeling to EEG complexity (Higuchi fractal dimension) in chronic pain patients. Larger negative deviations from healthy norms, particularly in frontal regions, were significantly correlated with higher pain intensity, suggesting that normative deviation mapping of EEG complexity could serve as a marker for chronic pain severity.

papers.title: Combined MEG and EEG suggest a limbic source network of the P3 including retrosplenial cortex and hippocampus
papers.summary: This study combined MEG and EEG source analysis with an extended source space including hippocampus, finding that the P3 component arises from a limbic network including retrosplenial cortex and hippocampus, with subsequent insula and cingulate activity, and simulations supporting the source combination.

papers.title: EEG Microstate Sequences as Potential Brain-Computer Interface Triggers Derived from Motor Imagery Classification
papers.summary: The study investigated EEG microstate sequences as potential BCI triggers based on motor imagery classification, using an LSTM-based autoencoder and dense neural network. Transfer learning achieved peak classification accuracies around 89%, with an average of 400 seconds needed for calibration to reach 80% accuracy.

papers.title: Unraveling the protective effect of weekend catch-up sleep on overactive bladder risk.
papers.summary: This study analyzed NHANES data to examine the association between weekend catch-up sleep (WCS) and overactive bladder (OAB) risk. It found a U-shaped relationship with a turning point at 1.5 hours, suggesting that moderate WCS (within 1.5h) is linked to reduced OAB prevalence and severity.

papers.title: Graph convolution neural network channel selection with attention for motor imagery EEG decoding.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a graph neural network-based co-optimization framework for simultaneous channel selection and MI classification in EEG-based BCIs. The method achieves performance comparable to using all channels with significantly fewer electrodes and surpasses current state-of-the-art models on multiple datasets.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm of heart rate variability in tropical horses: age-associated autonomic alterations and environmental air pollution effects in an urban field setting.
papers.summary: This field study characterized 24-hour heart rate variability patterns in tropical horses, finding blunted circadian autonomic modulation, age-related reductions in parasympathetic activity, and negative correlations between air pollution (PM2.5, AQI) and HRV indices. It provides first evidence linking ambient air pollution with resting HRV alterations in horses.

papers.title: Chronotype distinctness a key risk factor for emotional and cognitive disruption in shift working nurses
papers.summary: This study used structural equation modeling to explore how sleep and chronotype distinctness affect neuropsychiatric symptoms in shift-working nurses. It found that in rotating-shift workers, chronotype distinctness was a key determinant of adverse effects like mood disorders and cognitive impairments, while sleep governed fatigue-based symptoms in day-shift workers.

papers.title: Residual cortical responses and network reorganization in inherited retinal degeneration: electrophysiological evidence
papers.summary: The study examined cortical responses in retinitis pigmentosa patients using SSVEPs and TMS-EEG. It found that visually driven activity weakens with eccentricity, but direct cortical perturbation reveals preserved and even enhanced reactivity, suggesting a homeostatic increase in cortical gain rather than uniform loss.

papers.title: Magnetoreceptive CRY/MagR complexes: linking circadian redox signalling to protein aggregation in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: This review examines magneto-proteins, particularly CRY/MagR-based magnetoreceptor complexes, and their potential intersections with Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease pathology. It synthesizes evidence suggesting these complexes may modulate oxidative stress, mitochondrial bioenergetics, protein aggregation, and circadian control, but notes that direct human validation remains limited.

papers.title: Impact of Sleep on Glucose Metabolism in Individuals With Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review.
papers.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
papers.summary: This systematic review of 18 studies including 7715 adults with BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2 found that sleep restriction and poor sleep quality are associated with reduced insulin sensitivity and adverse cardiometabolic outcomes, although findings for fasting glucose were inconsistent. The authors recommend integrating sleep optimization into metabolic health management for overweight/obese individuals.

papers.title: Behavioral Pain Interventions Improve Sleep via Reduced Pain Interference and Catastrophizing: Secondary Longitudinal Mediation Analysis.
papers.summary: Secondary longitudinal mediation analysis of a 3-arm randomized trial (N=223) in chronic low back pain tested whether changes in pain intensity, interference, catastrophizing, and self-efficacy explain sleep improvement from behavioral pain interventions. Reductions in pain interference and catastrophizing, but not pain intensity, mediated sleep improvement, suggesting these are candidate pathways for cross-domain benefits.

papers.title: The Tsuru Longitudinal Study: Design and Profile of Participants.
papers.summary: Describes the design and participant profile of the Tsuru Longitudinal Study, a cohort study of Japanese older adults (≥65 years) with repeated mail surveys, accelerometer-based physical behavior assessments, and linked administrative data. The study aims to examine associations of physical behaviors (physical activity, sedentary behavior, sleep) with health outcomes, with response rates ranging 63.6%-74.6% across waves.

papers.title: Dynamic Entropic Mapping of Alzheimer's Neuropathology: Eyes-Open and Eyes-Closed EEG Biomarkers through Wavelet Entropy Analysis.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study (N=60) applied eyes-open/eyes-closed wavelet entropy analysis to EEG in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and controls. AD patients showed reduced alpha entropy differences between states, and occipital ΔENα correlated with MMSE (r=0.9000, p<0.001), indicating potential as a noninvasive EEG biomarker for early AD detection.

papers.title: Sleep disturbance in CKD: patient‑prioritized outcomes, management, and perceptions - a multicenter mixed-methods study in Australia.
papers.summary: Multicenter mixed-methods study in Australia (N=234 survey, 14 interviews) explored sleep disturbance in CKD stage 4-5. 73% were poor sleepers, with fragmented sleep and nocturia most common; 41% reported clinicians never asked about sleep, and management (often pharmacological) did not align with patient preferences for nonpharmacological approaches.

papers.title: Evaluating computational assays of chronic fatigue using UK Biobank data
papers.summary: Using UK Biobank data from over 2,200 participants, this study evaluated computational assays of chronic fatigue via machine learning on clinical and neuroimaging data. Clinical data alone achieved 61% balanced accuracy, and adding brain connectivity improved to 64%, but not consistently; sleep-related features, especially insomnia, were the most important predictors.

papers.title: The Chain Mediating Effect of Sleep Quality and Family Resilience Between Depressive Mood and Treatment Compliance in Continuous Blood Purification Patients.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 195 continuous blood purification patients used mediation analysis to show that depressive mood is associated with poorer sleep quality and lower family resilience, which in turn are associated with lower treatment compliance. The chain mediation effect accounted for 41.74% of the total effect, suggesting sleep quality and family resilience as potential intervention targets.

papers.title: Relationships Between Coping Flexibility, Distress, and Bedtime Procrastination: A Longitudinal Study.
papers.summary: This longitudinal study of 154 college students found that higher coping flexibility was associated with lower bedtime procrastination one year later, mediated by reduced distress. The findings suggest that interventions to enhance coping flexibility may reduce bedtime procrastination.

papers.title: The Glymphatic System in α-Synucleinopathies.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence linking glymphatic system dysfunction to α-synucleinopathies, including Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, and multiple system atrophy. It highlights impaired glymphatic clearance as a potential contributor to pathogenesis and discusses therapeutic strategies to enhance it.

papers.title: A Baseline Prediction Model for First-Year CPAP Treatment Disengagement in Adults with Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Secondary Analysis of a Danish Cohort.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of 662 Danish CPAP patients developed and internally validated a baseline prediction model for first-year treatment disengagement using current smoking, Epworth Sleepiness Scale score, and apnea-hypopnea index, achieving a cross-validated AUC of 0.762. The model provides a benchmark for external validation in contemporary cohorts.

papers.title: Prevalence and Risk of Mild Cognitive Impairment Among Chinese Adults Aged 60 Years and Above: A Cross-Sectional Study Based on National Data.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 694 older Chinese adults found a mild cognitive impairment (MCI) prevalence of 14.54%. Elevated depression score, rural residence, napping, female sex, and poor memory were identified as independent risk factors for MCI.

papers.title: From couch to Ironman 70.3: A three-year case study of weight loss and cardiometabolic adaptation revealed through continuous wearable monitoring.
papers.summary: This single-participant case study used 1,146 days of continuous wearable monitoring to document a 27.8% weight loss and Ironman 70.3 completion in a young adult male. Improvements in resting heart rate, HRV, clinical biomarkers, and cardiorespiratory fitness were observed, illustrating the potential of long-term wearables to capture behavior-driven cardiometabolic changes.

papers.title: The Role of Mirtazapine in the Pathogenesis and Therapy of Chronic Liver Disease.
papers.summary: This review examines the dual role of mirtazapine in chronic liver disease, highlighting its potential anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic effects in preclinical models, while also acknowledging its metabolic adverse effects such as weight gain and insulin resistance. The authors emphasize the need to balance benefits and risks when prescribing to patients with comorbid depression.

papers.title: Beyond the Mouth: Oral Health-Related Quality of Life and Emotional Loneliness in Later Life and Their Associations With Sleep Quality and Dream Recall.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 609 Greek older adults found that better oral health-related quality of life was associated with lower emotional loneliness and better sleep quality, but the association with dream recall was weak and considered exploratory. The authors caution that causal conclusions cannot be drawn and call for replication with validated measures.

papers.title: Influencing Factors and Prediction Model Construction of Anxiety and Depression in Patients With Coronary Heart Disease Undergoing In-Stent Restenosis.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 256 patients with in-stent restenosis found high prevalence of anxiety (37.89%) and depression (42.58%). Independent risk factors included sleep quality, social support, NYHA class, number of stents, and residence area for anxiety; and age, sleep quality, social support, stents, and Mehran classification for depression. Nomograms showed good predictive accuracy (AUC 0.79 and 0.82).

papers.title: Sleep duration and tiredness at school from childhood to adolescence: repeated surveys over 10 years in Swedish schoolchildren.
papers.journal: Journal of research in nursing : JRN
papers.summary: This repeated survey study across 10 years in Swedish schoolchildren found that insufficient sleep prevalence rose from below 10% at ages 6-10 to 31% at age 14 and 74% at age 16, and shorter sleep was associated with increased tiredness at school.

papers.title: Refractory Hyperammonemic Encephalopathy as a Paraneoplastic Presentation of Fibrolamellar Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Case Report.
papers.journal: The American journal of case reports
papers.summary: This case report describes a 24-year-old man with metastatic fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma who developed refractory hyperammonemic encephalopathy due to an acquired urea cycle disorder, indicated by depleted urea cycle intermediates and elevated urinary orotic acid. Despite treatment with ammonia scavengers and renal replacement therapy, the patient died, highlighting the poor prognosis and need for early multidisciplinary and palliative care.

papers.title: Risk Factors for Postoperative Sleep Disturbance in Elderly Patients Undergoing Hip Arthroplasty Surgery: The Role of Preoperative Depression and Anxiety.
papers.summary: This case-control study of 204 elderly hip arthroplasty patients identified preoperative anxiety and depression, postoperative day 1 pain, and longer time to first ambulation as independent risk factors for postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD). Preoperative anxiety and postoperative pain showed a significant synergistic interaction.

papers.title: Prevalence of Anxiety and Depression Among Patients in a Palliative Care Setting During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Mixed-Methods Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: This mixed-methods cross-sectional study of 96 palliative care patients in Uganda during the COVID-19 pandemic found high rates of anxiety and depression, associated with income, missed appointments, and sleep changes. Qualitative themes revealed multidimensional suffering and the healthcare system as a precipitant, highlighting the need for integrated mental health support in emergencies.

papers.title: Computed Tomography-Based Evaluation of Positional Cranial Deformities in Emergency Department Patients Aged 15 to 39 Years in Japan.
papers.summary: This retrospective cross-sectional CT study of 242 Japanese adults aged 15-39 without intracranial abnormalities found a 53.3% prevalence of plagiocephaly (median CVAI 3.94) and 1.6% or 72.3% brachycephaly depending on reference criteria. The results suggest that positional cranial deformities remain common in Japanese young adults, are not fully explained by infant sleep positioning, and highlight the need for population-specific reference values.

papers.title: Microdebrider Adenoidectomy Technique.
papers.summary: This paper describes the microdebrider technique for adenoidectomy, highlighting its advantages (precise excision, clear visualization, reduced bleeding and regrowth) and disadvantages, and concludes that it is safe and effective, especially for experienced ENT surgeons. The technique is presented as an alternative to curettage, cautery, and coblation.

papers.title: Melatonin and Cortisol Concentration Before and After CPAP Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea [Retraction].
papers.summary: This is a retraction notice for the article DOI: 10.2147/NSS.S553499 titled 'Melatonin and Cortisol Concentration Before and After CPAP Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea'. It retracts that previously published article.

papers.title: Trajectory Patterns of Perioperative Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms in Patients With Digestive System Malignancies and Their Impact on Postoperative Outcomes.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study of 285 patients with digestive system malignancies identified three distinct perioperative anxiety and depressive symptom trajectories (resilient, recovery, chronic) using latent class growth analysis. The chronic trajectory was associated with higher inflammation markers, more complications, longer hospital stays, and lower recovery quality, with independent predictors including stage III disease and reduced social support.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
